speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what the vertigo feels like—does the room spin around you, or do you feel like you are spinning while the room stays still? Also, did this start suddenly while you were resting or did it begin after you moved your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear? Also, do the symptoms return if you move your head in specific directions, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the brief duration of symptoms and their onset during bed entry, I suspect a peripheral cause. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the left side is diagnostic for Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
